policy: Review every closed candidate set. Select only when ASV wording or an explicit mapped textual note distinguishes a reading; otherwise mark underdetermined and retain the base fallback. The base candidate is the qere, which is what MACULA Hebrew projects; the alternative is the ketiv written in the Leningrad Codex.

decisions.evidence: ASV reads the plural, 'for his mercies are great', rendering the qere plural rachamayw rather than the ketiv singular rachamo. The mapped note 'Or, many' is classed alternative_rendering and bears on the English adjective 'great', not on the number of the noun, so it does not decide the unit; the plural noun in the text does.

ASV's text names 'Araunah the Jebusite', which renders the qere ha-Aravnah; the ketiv ha-Ornah would give the form the ASV relegates to its margin. The note 'Or, Ornah. In 1 Chr. 21:15, Ornan' is classed alternative_rendering and so cannot select the ketiv; the reading is decided by the name standing in the ASV text.

ASV reads 'the threshing-floor of Araunah the Jebusite', matching the qere Aravnah; the ketiv Arniyah would yield a different name (Arniah/Ornan-like), which the ASV does not render here and does not note.

ASV renders the phrase idiomatically, 'what seemeth good unto him', without an English word for 'eyes' at all, so neither the qere plural be-'enayw nor the ketiv be-'eno is distinguished; both are the same idiom and yield identical English. No ASV note is mapped to this unit, so the base fallback (qere) carries the projection.
